Job Title: Project Manager, Large Projects CMD Commercial Job Location: Remote, California, United States of America Job Location Type: Remote Job Contract Type: Full time Job Seniority Level: Work Schedule: 40 hours per week Work Schedule First Shift (Days) Environmental Conditions Office Job Description Job Description As part of the Thermo Fisher Scientific team, you’ll discover meaningful work that makes a positive impact on a global scale.

Join our colleagues in bringing our Mission to life every single day to enable our customers to make the world healthier, cleaner and safer.

We provide our global teams with the resources needed to achieve individual career goals while helping to take science a step beyond by developing solutions for some of the world’s toughest challenges, like protecting the environment, making sure our food is safe or helping find cures for cancer.

DESCRIPTION: At Thermo Fisher Scientific, you'll manage complex strategic projects that make a meaningful impact on our mission to enable customers to make the world healthier, cleaner, and safer.

As Sr Project Manager, you'll guide successful execution of important initiatives across functions, ensuring timely delivery, risk mitigation, and stakeholder alignment.

You'll manage multiple high-priority projects simultaneously, coordinating cross-functional teams through the complete project lifecycle while maintaining focus on business objectives and quality standards.

Your expertise will be instrumental in implementing process improvements, new technologies, and transformational changes that enhance operational efficiency and customer success.

Project Manager – Large Projects Administrative Project Management Focus Position Summary The Project Manager – Large Projects is responsible for the administrative coordination, governance, documentation, tracking, and reporting required to support large, complex projects.

This role ensures that project information is organized, timelines are visible, actions are tracked, risks and issues are documented, and stakeholders have accurate information to support decision-making. This role does not own solution design, deployment strategy, customer adoption, operational readiness, or business execution.

Instead, the Project Manager provides the structure, cadence, documentation, and administrative discipline needed to keep large projects organized and transparent.

This is an individual contributor role that works closely with project sponsors, workstream owners, Solution Deployment Leaders, commercial teams, operations, finance, legal, quality, supply chain, digital, and other stakeholders.

Key Responsibilities: Project Administration and Coordination Maintain project plans, timelines, milestones, action trackers, decision logs, risk logs, issue logs, and dependency trackers. Coordinate project meetings, governance forums, steering committee reviews, and stakeholder update sessions.

Prepare meeting agendas, capture minutes, document decisions, and follow up on assigned actions. Ensure project documentation is complete, current, organized, and accessible to appropriate stakeholders. Support consistent use of project templates, tools, trackers, and reporting formats.

Governance Support Support project governance by maintaining meeting cadence, escalation records, approval documentation, and decision history. Track required approvals, sign-offs, stage gates, and governance checkpoints. Ensure project sponsors and workstream owners have accurate information for reviews and decisions.

Maintain visibility to open decisions, overdue actions, unresolved issues, and upcoming milestones. Help ensure governance processes are followed consistently across large projects. Timeline and Milestone Tracking Maintain the master project timeline based on input from workstream owners and accountable business leads.

Track progress against milestones, deliverables, and agreed due dates. Identify and flag timeline variances, overdue items, and dependency gaps for review by accountable owners. Consolidate updates from multiple workstreams into a single project view. Support visibility to critical path items without owning execution of the underlying work.

Reporting and Communication Support Prepare project status reports, dashboards, executive summaries, and stakeholder updates. Consolidate inputs from workstream owners, deployment leaders, finance, operations, commercial teams, and other functions.

Ensure project reports clearly reflect status, milestones, risks, issues, decisions needed, and next steps. Maintain accurate records of project communications and leadership updates. Support consistent and timely information flow across project stakeholders. Risk, Issue, and Action Tracking Maintain risk, issue, action, and dependency logs.

Document risk descriptions, issue status, owners, target dates, mitigation updates, and escalation history. Follow up with accountable owners to obtain updates and closure status. Flag overdue actions, unresolved issues, or missing information to project sponsors or designated leads.

Support escalation documentation but does not own resolution of technical, operational, commercial, or deployment issues. Budget and Resource Administration Track project budget information, purchase orders, invoices, resource assumptions, and financial updates as directed by finance or project sponsors.

Consolidate budget and resource inputs for project reporting. Maintain documentation related to project spend, approvals, forecasts, and financial decisions. Support administrative coordination of vendor documentation, contracts, statements of work, and related records.

Flag missing financial information, pending approvals, or budget variances for review by accountable owners. Documentation and Records Management Maintain organized project repositories, files, version control, and document naming standards.

Ensure key project documents, approvals, meeting records, reports, and governance materials are stored appropriately. Support audit readiness by maintaining clear records of decisions, approvals, risks, changes, and status updates. Capture lessons learned and archive project materials at project close.

Support continuous improvement of project administration tools, templates, and documentation practices. Required Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in business, operations, project management, life sciences, engineering, or related field preferred.

Experience supporting large projects, complex initiatives, project management offices, commercial operations, business operations, or administrative project coordination. Strong skills in project documentation, meeting coordination, status reporting, action tracking, and records management.

Ability to consolidate information from multiple stakeholders into clear, accurate project updates. Strong organizational skills and attention to detail. Ability to manage multiple deadlines, documents, trackers, and reporting cycles. Strong written and verbal communication skills.

Proficiency with project management, collaboration, reporting, and productivity tools. Ability to work in a matrixed organization and follow up with stakeholders across functions and levels. Preferred Qualifications Experience supporting large customer, commercial, operational, supply chain, digital, or transformation projects.

Experience in life sciences, pharmaceutical, biopharma, healthcare, diagnostics, laboratory, manufacturing, or regulated environments. Familiarity with project governance, PMO practices, stage-gate processes, and executive reporting.

Experience with tools such as Microsoft Project, Smartsheet, Excel, PowerPoint, SharePoint, Teams, Power BI, CRM, ERP, or similar platforms. Understanding of budget tracking, purchase order processes, vendor documentation, or contract administration. Project management certification or training preferred but not required.

Key Competencies Project administration Documentation management Meeting coordination Status reporting Timeline tracking Action-item follow-up Risk and issue logging Governance support Records management Attention to detail Stakeholder follow-up Tool and tracker discipline Scope and Impact The Project Manager – Large Projects is an individual contributor role focused on the administrative management of large, complex projects.

The role supports project transparency, governance discipline, documentation quality, leadership visibility, and timely follow-up. The role does not own solution deployment, customer adoption, operational readiness, business execution, technical solution design, or commercial strategy.

Accountability for those activities remains with designated business owners, Solution Deployment Leaders, Solution Architects, commercial leaders, and functional teams. Travel Requirements Limited travel may be required for project meetings, governance sessions, workshops, or site-based coordination.

Compensation and Benefits The salary range estimated for this position based in California is $112,500.00–$168,500.00. This position may also be eligible to receive a variable annual bonus based on company, team, and/or individual performance results in accordance with company policy.

We offer a comprehensive Total Rewards package that our U.S. colleagues and their families can count on, which includes: A choice of national medical and dental plans, and a national vision plan, including health incentive programs Employee assistance and family support programs, including commuter benefits and tuition reimbursement At least 120 hours paid time off (PTO), 10 paid holidays annually, paid parental leave (3 weeks for bonding and 8 weeks for caregiver leave), accident and life insurance, and short- and long-term disability in accordance with company policy Retirement and savings programs, such as our competitive 401(k) U.S. retirement savings plan Employees’ Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP) offers eligible colleagues the opportunity to purchase company stock at a discount For more information on our benefits, please visit: https://jobs.thermofisher.com/global/en/total-rewards This job is curated by Lifelancer .

AmeriSave Mortgage Corp. has set the standard in online mortgage lending, with over $130 billion in funded loan volume. As one of the top rated, largest privately owned online mortgage lenders in the nation, our mission is to deliver beneficial, responsible home lending solutions with unwavering integrity, dedication and excellence.

We leverage cutting edge technology and data driven strategies to provide exceptional service to our customers. Our employees are the driving force behind our success. We believe in the power of a dynamic and talented workforce and creating an environment where your contributions are not just recognized, they're celebrated.

Your success is our success, and we are seeking skilled professionals who are ready to bring their A-game, exceed benchmarks, and enhance the overall excellence of AmeriSave, while also growing and advancing their careers. At AmeriSave, we're one team with one shared dream: to be the best. Let's redefine excellence together!

What We’re Looking For: AmeriSave is seeking a Senior Project Manager to join our Enterprise Technology & AI organization. This role sits at the intersection of technology and the business, driving complex, cross-functional initiatives that span in-house built systems, operational process change, and executive-level strategic priorities.

This is a high-visibility role for someone who has led both technology projects and business initiatives end to end, ideally within a well-known mortgage lending organization, and who is equally comfortable in a Gantt chart, a stakeholder steering committee, or a working session with engineers reviewing a build.

You will be the connective tissue between technology, operations, and leadership, translating strategy into executable plans and keeping delivery honest with data.

What You'll Do: End-to-End Project Ownership: Own the full lifecycle of complex, cross-functional projects, from charter and requirements through execution, go-live, and post-launch measurement, spanning both technology builds and business/operational initiatives.

In-House Technology Delivery: Manage delivery of technology projects built in-house by internal engineering teams, partnering closely with product, engineering, and QA to sequence work, manage dependencies, and de-risk timelines for custom-built platforms and tools.

Planning & Tooling: Build and maintain detailed project plans, roadmaps, and Gantt charts using modern project management tooling; track milestones, critical path, resourcing, and risk in a way that is transparent to both delivery teams and executives.

Cross-Functional Leadership: Lead project teams composed of stakeholders across Technology, Operations, Capital Markets, Compliance, and Customer Service; align competing priorities, resolve blockers, and drive decisions to closure across departmental lines.

Executive Communication: Prepare and deliver clear, concise, and data-backed status updates, business cases, and executive readouts; comfortably present progress, risks, and trade-offs directly to senior leadership and C-suite stakeholders.

Analytical Rigor: Use data to drive decisions: define success metrics up front, build reporting/dashboards to track project and post-launch performance, and use quantitative analysis to identify risk, scope creep, or underperformance early.

Process Improvement: Identify process gaps and inefficiencies across the project portfolio and drive continuous improvement in how the organization plans, prioritizes, and delivers work.

Risk Management: Proactively surface, document, and manage project risks and issues, escalating appropriately and driving mitigation plans to protect timelines and business outcomes.

What You’ll Need: Deep Industry Experience: 7+ years of project management experience leading both technology and business initiatives, preferably within the mortgage industry, and preferably with a well-known mortgage lender or financial services company.

Technology & Business Project Management: Demonstrated success managing technology projects built in-house (custom platforms, internal tools, proprietary systems) in close partnership with engineering teams, in addition to managing business/operational projects.

Tools & Planning: Advanced proficiency with project management tools (e.g., Smartsheet, MS Project, Jira, Asana, or similar) and hands-on skill building and maintaining Gantt charts, roadmaps, and resourcing plans.

Cross-Functional Project Management: Proven track record managing initiatives across multiple departments and stakeholder groups, building consensus and driving alignment among teams with competing priorities.

Executive Communication: Polished, confident communicator who can distill complex, technical, or ambiguous initiatives into clear narratives for executive audiences, both in writing and in live presentations.

Analytical Mindset: Comfortable working with data to define KPIs, build simple dashboards or reporting views, and use metrics (not just status colors) to tell the true story of a project's health. Certifications: PMP, PgMP, or equivalent certification a plus; experience with Agile/Scrum delivery models is a requirement.

Education: Bachelor's degree in Business, Technology, Finance, or a related field; MBA a plus. High-speed internet required for remote work, Cable or Fiber ONLY with the ability to connect via Ethernet.

Minimum speeds: 70/30 Mbps (basic), 200-300/35-70 Mbps (shared), 500-1,000/100+ Mbps (heavy use). **Please note that the compensation and benefit information that follows is a good faith estimate for this position only and is provided pursuant to applicable state and local laws on pay transparency.

It is estimated based on what a successful applicant in the relevant state might be paid. ** Compensation: The annual compensation for this position generally ranges from between $120,000 – $160,000 based on experience and qualifications.

Gleichzeitig vertreten Sie den Zürcher Tierschutz gegenüber Medien, Politik, Behörden und Partnerorganisationen und wirken aktiv an der Weiterentwicklung der Gesamtorganisation mit.

* Konzeption und Steuerung von Tierschutz- und Aufklärungskampagnen in Zusammenarbeit mit Marketing & Kommunikation

Sie verfügen über eine höhere Ausbildung (FH/Universität) oder eine vergleichbare Qualifikation sowie über mehrjährige Führungserfahrung, idealerweise in einer NGO. The Service Delivery Manager is responsible for coordinating the successful delivery of customer projects and service engagements by aligning resource capacity with customer demand, driving project execution, and ensuring delivery commitments are met. This role serves as the operational hub between customers, delivery teams, project resources, and leadership to ensure projects are properly staffed, risks are proactively managed, and customer expectations are consistently achieved.
The Service Delivery Manager oversees project governance, resource planning, meeting facilitation, action item management, and escalation resolution while maintaining visibility into project health, resource utilization, timelines, budgets, and overall customer satisfaction.
You will lead end-to-end delivery of Palantir-based programs, ensuring alignment between stakeholders, timelines, and technical teams. Role Description
Resource Management & Capacity Planning
Maintain visibility into all available service delivery resources and project assignments.
Align inbound project demand with available resource capacity and skill sets.
Coordinate resource assignments across multiple customer engagements and projects.
Monitor resource utilization and recommend adjustments to optimize delivery performance.
Identify resource constraints and skill gaps and develop mitigation plans.
Partner with delivery leaders and functional managers on staffing priorities and future resource needs.
Project Delivery & Execution
Track all incoming projects and service engagements from initiation through completion.
Ensure projects are appropriately staffed and aligned to customer requirements.
Monitor project schedules, milestones, budgets, risks, and deliverables.
Facilitate project status meetings, delivery reviews, and customer update meetings.
Ensure projects remain on track and proactively address obstacles impacting delivery.
Support project teams in developing and executing recovery plans when necessary.
Governance & Accountability
Facilitate recurring project and operational review meetings.
Document meeting outcomes, decisions, action items, owners, and due dates.
Distribute meeting notes within established timelines.
Track action items through completion and hold stakeholders accountable for commitments.
Maintain project dashboards, status reports, risk logs, and delivery metrics.
Ensure consistent adherence to delivery processes and governance standards.
Risk & Escalation Management
Identify and manage project risks related to scope, budget, timeline, resources, and technical dependencies.
Maintain risk and issue logs for active projects.
Work with project teams to develop mitigation plans and corrective actions.
Serve as the primary escalation point for project delivery and resource-related issues.
Drive issue resolution while maintaining alignment among stakeholders.
Escalate significant risks and concerns to leadership when appropriate.
Customer & Stakeholder Management
Build strong working relationships with customer stakeholders and internal teams.
Provide clear communication regarding project status, risks, resource challenges, and delivery commitments.
Facilitate discussions to resolve competing priorities and delivery challenges.
Support customer satisfaction through proactive communication and successful execution.
Ensure customer expectations are aligned with project objectives and delivery capabilities.
Behaviors and Competencies
Teamwork: Can work effectively in a team, contributing ideas and effort, and respecting the contributions of others.
Customer Service: Can identify customer needs, propose suitable solutions, and handle more complex customer interactions.
Organization: Can prioritize daily tasks, manage personal workflow, and utilize basic tools to keep track of responsibilities.
Time Management: Can generally use time effectively but may occasionally struggle with prioritizing tasks, meeting deadlines, or maintaining work-life balance.
Communication: Can effectively communicate complex ideas and information, and can adapt communication style to the audience.
Analytical Thinking: Can apply critical thinking to analyze data, identify patterns, and make basic inferences.
Problem-Solving: Can identify problems, propose solutions, and take action to resolve them without explicit instructions.
Detail-Oriented: Can identify errors or inconsistencies in work and make necessary corrections.
Presenting: Can prepare and deliver presentations, addressing key points and responding to questions with clarity.
Self-Motivation: Can identify personal or professional growth opportunities, propose self-improvement strategies, and take action without explicit instructions.
Negotiation: Can identify opportunities for compromise, propose solutions, and take action to influence outcomes without explicit instructions.
Initiative: Can identify opportunities for improvement, propose solutions, and take action without explicit instructions.
Consultative Sales: Can identify customer needs, propose suitable products or services, and take action to close sales without explicit instructions.
